title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics and tool message formatting + schema mapping tweaks
author: Sofia Martinez
description: Context: The OpenAI compatibility layer currently supports function/tool calling and basic schema mapping, but we have observed inconsistencies around how 'tool_choice' is emitted and how downstream tool messages are formatted. Motivation: align Redwood's openai-compat output with OpenAI's documented semantics for 'tool_choice' (choice metadata, index vs name handling), and produce a stable, unambiguous tool message format that downstream connectors and SDKs can parse without special-casing. This change also tightens schema mapping behavior so that ambiguous member names do not silently drop data. Summary of changes: 1) tool_choice: emit a consistent object with 'name' and 'metadata' keys and include the original model-provided index in 'metadata.index' when available. We deliberately avoid exposing internal server ids. 2) Message formatting: tool-invocation messages are now emitted as role="tool" with content set to the serialized tool response. For structured responses we include a 'content_type' hint in the message metadata (e.g., application/json) to aid SDKs that previously relied on brittle heuristics. 3) Schema mapping: tighten mapping rules to prefer explicit mappings on tool registration, fall back to name-based mapping only when unambiguous, and log a debug-level warning when mapping choices are ambiguous. 4) Backwards compatibility: add a compatibility flag (OPENAI_COMPAT_LEGACY_TOOL_CHOICE) which, when enabled, preserves the legacy flattened string choice format for customers requiring it. Default remains the new, spec-aligned format. 5) Tests and docs: add unit/integration tests covering tool_choice permutations, streaming tool messages, and schema collisions; update openai-compat README and API docs with examples and migration notes. Checklist: - [x] Implement tool_choice object emission and metadata.index population - [x] Produce consistent tool message formatting for role=tool and content_type hints - [x] Add compatibility flag and backward-compatibility tests - [x] Update docs and examples in redwood-openai-compat - [x] Add unit and integration tests (including streaming scenarios) - [x] Run perf bench to ensure no regression on median latency Notes on implementation: - The compat layer now maps model "tool call" tokens to a ToolChoice struct that serializes to the OpenAI-compatible object. The index is included under metadata.index only when the model provides it; otherwise metadata.index is omitted to avoid confusion. - Tool messages emitted during streaming are buffered into logical tool message frames; frames are flushed as role=tool delta events and as a final aggregated role=tool message for non-streaming clients. - To avoid regressions in high-throughput serving, message serialization is implemented as an allocation-minimal path that reuses buffer pools already used by the streaming runtime. - Schema mapping changes live behind a feature-guard and are enabled by default; ambiguous mapping now triggers a debug log with a Linear ticket suggestion to register explicit mapping. Testing and CI: - Added unit tests for 8 distinct tool_choice permutations (name+index, name-only, index-only, name collision scenarios). - Integration tests simulate model-provided choice + tool execution roundtrip via the openai-compat HTTP shim and the runtime streaming layer. - Benchmarks: micro-benchmarks show <1% median latency regression; tail p99 unchanged. Migration notes for customers: - Most customers see no changes. If you relied on parsing a flattened "tool_choice" string in the compat layer, set OPENAI_COMPAT_LEGACY_TOOL_CHOICE=true while updating clients. - If you register tools with ambiguous names, consider adding explicit schema mapping entries to avoid the new debug warnings. Related work: closes ENG-2314, references PRs pr-35789 (streaming stability) and pr-35890 (tool-choice schema message formatting), and links to the openai-compat docs update in redwood-docs. CI: all checks passing (see ci_checks). Merge: squash-merged into main after approvals.
commits: feat(openai-compat): emit tool_choice as object with name + metadata.index
refactor(compat): unify tool message serialization path for streaming and non-streaming
fix(schema-mapping): prefer explicit mappings and warn on ambiguity
test(openai-compat): add unit + integration tests for tool_choice permutations
docs(openai-compat): update README and examples for new tool_choice format
review_comments: Evan Liu: Please ensure the index is only added when the model provides it. We had a bug earlier where index=0 was interpreted as missing and dropped.
Sofia Martinez: Addressed - index is added only when present and we serialize it as an integer under metadata.index. Updated tests to include index=0 case.
Priya Kapoor: Can the content_type hint be optional? Some SDKs may not consume it and adding it could break strict parsers.
Sofia Martinez: content_type is an optional metadata hint; when absent we default to text/plain. Updated docs to describe parser behavior.
Dominic Reyes: Performance looks good in microbenchmarks, but add a canary rollout plan to avoid coupling issues with older SDKs.
Sofia Martinez: Added rollout notes and legacy flag; will coordinate a canary on dedicated and hosted before full rollout.
merge_summary: Squash-merged after 3 approvals. No outstanding change requests. Feature-guard enabled by default; compatibility flag available for legacy parsing.
release_notes: OpenAI compatibility: tool calling behavior updated. tool_choice is now emitted as an object { name, metadata } (metadata.index included when available). Tool messages are standardized with role=tool and an optional content_type hint. Schema mapping made stricter to avoid silent collisions. Backwards-compatibility flag OPENAI_COMPAT_LEGACY_TOOL_CHOICE available.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: clients that parsed legacy flattened tool_choice strings may break. Mitigation: compatibility flag, docs, and migration examples. We will run a staged canary on hosted and Dedicated clusters and monitor errors for 72h before full rollout.
notes_for_release_manager: Coordinate canary rollout with platform infra. Notify SDK teams and docs maintainers. Monitor openai-compat error budget and model-serving logs for mapping warnings (ENG-2314).
